reasoning: This question asks whether federal spending will decrease by more than $250 billion between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025. Key considerations: (1) Federal spending typically grows year-over-year due to inflation, population growth, and mandatory spending increases; (2) DOGE (Department of Government Efficiency) was created to identify cuts, but actual implementation faces Congressional constraints; (3) A $250B decrease would require reversing normal spending growth plus achieving significant cuts—historically difficult; (4) While Trump administration has cut-focused rhetoric, achieving net spending reductions of this magnitude in one year is rare; (5) Mandatory spending (Social Security, Medicare) is hard to cut; (6) Political feasibility of large cuts remains uncertain. The baseline expectation is spending growth, not contraction.
